lines_of_business: Health benefit plans administered by Cigna Companies; plan document supersedes; federal/state mandates for lymphedema may govern
effective_or_revised: Effective Date 5/15/2026; Next Review Date 4/15/2027 (Coverage Policy 0354, titled 'Compression Devices')
criteria_location: Coverage Policy pp.2-3 (about 1.5 pages): standard device, calibrated gradient device, continuation, experimental, not covered. Rest is coding, background, literature.
procedures_covered: Standard pneumatic compression device E0650/E0651 and appliances
Calibrated gradient pressure E0652 and appliances
E0675 arterial insufficiency, E0676 intermittent limb device, cooling pneumatic devices (Game Ready, C9817) - not covered

logic.top_level: pathways: two indications (lymphedema OR CVI with ulcer) for standard device; E0652 as AND over standard criteria and an OR of two

k_of_n.quote: medically necessary for EITHER of the following: for the treatment of intractable lymphedema ... for the treatment of chronic venous insufficiency (CVI) with venous stasis ulcer(s)

logic.exclusions_or_contraindications: 'NOT COVERED OR REIMBURSABLE' and 'EXPERIMENTAL' lists by code; 'Pneumatic compression devices used in the home setting are not covered or reimbursable if the above criteria are not met.'
logic.initial_vs_repeat: 'Continuation of Use' with BOTH adherence and clinical improvement.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: for the treatment of intractable lymphedema when there is failure of a four-week trial of conservative medical management including ALL of the following: home exercise program, limb elevation, compression bandage or compression garment use
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Rendered with ALL in caps but items 'compression bandage or compression garment' contain an inner OR.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: EITHER of the following: documented failure of relief with standard pneumatic compression device; individual requires specified pressure to a localized area
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: The 'localized pressure' option does not require prior failure of standard device in the text, only that standard criteria were met.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Coverage for pneumatic compression devices/lymphedema pumps and cryotherapy machines varies across plans.
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Benefit variation precedes the criteria; whether criteria apply depends on the plan.

requirement_kinds.quote: for the treatment of intractable lymphedema
failure of a four-week trial of conservative medical management including ALL of the following: home exercise program; limb elevation; compression bandage or compression garment use
medically-supervised treatment of the ulcer(s) for at least 24 weeks using standard wound care treatment, including compression, wound dressings, exercise, and elevation
Failure of the ulcer(s) to decrease in size or demonstrate improvement despite conventional therapy.
documented failure of relief with standard pneumatic compression device; individual requires specified pressure to a localized area
there is adherence with the use of equipment as ordered by the healthcare professional
clinical documentation ... confirms clinical improvement (e.g., improvement in venous stasis ulcers, decrease in edema or lymphedema)

time_windows.quote: failure of a four-week trial of conservative medical management
at least 24 weeks using standard wound care treatment

codes.codes_tied_to_criteria: Criteria cite HCPCS ranges (e.g., 'E0655, E0660, E0665-E0669, E0671-E0673'); ICD-10 table lists covered diagnoses and says all other codes are not covered, i.e. diagnosis code is itself a coverage gate.
codes.non_covered_code_lists: E0677-E0683, E1399 experimental; E0675, E0676, C9817 not covered; 'All other codes' ICD not covered.

external_dependencies.quote: coverage for the treatment of lymphedema, including lymphedema pumps, may be governed by federal and/or state mandates
In certain markets, delegated vendor guidelines may be used to support medical necessity
(International Society of Lymphology, 2023; Ridner, et al., 2012 ...)

definitions_that_change_meaning.term: E0652 segmented device with calibrated gradient pressure
definitions_that_change_meaning.definition_quote: characterized by a manual control on at least three outflow ports that can deliver individually determined pressure to each segmental unit
either (a) the same pressure is present in each segment, or (b) there is a predetermined pressure gradient

vague_terms.problem: Undefined; no stage or skin finding.
Undefined for CVI beyond 'standard wound care treatment'.

vague_terms.quote: requires specified pressure to a localized area
vague_terms.problem: Background explains scarring/contracture but criterion text does not.

extraction_hazards: Long ICD-10 ranges with hyphens (L97.111-L97.119) and 'All other codes' rows spanning page breaks.
Criteria nested with private-use bullet glyphs (sub-bullets for ALL-of lists become plain lines).
Instructions for Use is a half page of boilerplate before the criteria.
Coverage statement also covers cryotherapy but the criteria do not (only 'not covered').
Background Literature Review carries clinical statements that could be mistaken for criteria (e.g., E0652 use for trunk edema).
interesting_structures: Two disease pathways (lymphedema, CVI ulcer) in one policy.
Diagnosis code table acts as a coverage gate.
Explicit 24 week wound-care requirement for CVI.
No stage, no trunk-specific criteria (BCBSFL/BCBSM have these).

fit_to_tree.why: Short all/any with two pathways; the strain comes from undefined 'intractable', 'failure', and ICD-code gating.
